title: Thumbs up? Sentiment Classification using Machine Learning Techniques
venue: Proceedings of the 2002 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2002)
research_note: Foundational supervised sentiment classification: compares machine-learning methods using lexical features. Useful for explaining why opinion classification differs from topic classification.
qualification: Foundational; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: Thumbs Up or Thumbs Down? Semantic Orientation Applied to Unsupervised Classification of Reviews
venue: Proceedings of the 40th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
research_note: Early semantic-orientation method based on phrase associations with positive and negative reference terms. Useful historical contrast to supervised classifiers.
qualification: Foundational; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: Baselines and Bigrams: Simple, Good Sentiment and Topic Classification
venue: Proceedings of the 50th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)
research_note: Demonstrates the importance of word bigrams, Naive Bayes variants, and NB-SVM. The most useful paper here for defining a strong classical baseline.
qualification: Core reading; methods/results inspected; historical comparison.

title: VADER: A Parsimonious Rule-Based Model for Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text
research_note: VADER combines a sentiment lexicon with rules tailored to social-media language. Useful for explaining rule-based sentiment and score thresholds.
qualification: Core lexicon source; publisher page inspected.

title: Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary w/ Sentiment Word Lists
research_note: Official financial dictionary resource, covering sentiment and other financial tone categories. Pair with the original journal paper R36.
qualification: Official resource rather than a separate research paper.

title: Good Debt or Bad Debt: Detecting Semantic Orientations in Economic Texts
research_note: Introduces the human-annotated financial phrase-bank and domain-aware semantic-orientation modeling. Relevant to label ambiguity and finance-specific evaluation.
qualification: 2013 preprint of work published in 2014; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: SemEval-2014 Task 4: Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis
venue: Proceedings of the 8th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation (SemEval 2014)
research_note: Defines aspect-based sentiment tasks that distinguish extracting aspects from predicting polarity for a known aspect. Useful for explaining why document polarity is insufficient.
qualification: Benchmark/task paper; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: Recursive Deep Models for Semantic Compositionality Over a Sentiment Treebank
venue: Proceedings of the 2013 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
research_note: Introduces the Stanford Sentiment Treebank and recursive compositional sentiment models. Useful background on phrase-level labels and composition.
qualification: Foundational neural method/dataset; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification
venue: Proceedings of the 2014 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
research_note: A CNN classifier using pretrained word embeddings. Useful example of learned local phrase features before the transformer era.
qualification: Neural method; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, Volume 1 (Long and Short Papers)
research_note: BERT contextual pretraining and fine-tuning. Useful technical foundation for the encoder-classifier family; it is not a sentiment-only model.
qualification: Transformer foundation; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
research_note: Knowledge distillation into a smaller BERT-family model. Useful for discussing compact contextual models and inference efficiency.
qualification: 2019 preprint; abstract/metadata inspected; no local timing reproduction.

title: FinBERT: Financial Sentiment Analysis with Pre-trained Language Models
research_note: Financial sentiment classification using BERT. Strong middle-category reference, with Financial PhraseBank and FiQA evaluation. Its baseline-tuning caveat matters when interpreting results.
qualification: Core reading; 2019 thesis/preprint; methods/results inspected.

title: Sentiment Analysis in the Era of Large Language Models: A Reality Check
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024
research_note: Broad evaluation over 13 tasks and 26 datasets, including limited-label settings and structured sentiment extraction. The main comparative LLM reference, with explicit old-model and English-only limitations.
qualification: Core reading; cite NAACL Findings 2024 publication, not only its 2023 preprint; methods/results/limitations inspected.

title: Is ChatGPT a Good Sentiment Analyzer? A Preliminary Study
research_note: Evaluates ChatGPT on sentiment, opinions, and emotions, including standard, polarity-shift, and open-domain settings. Useful complementary evaluation dimensions.
qualification: 2023 preprint, revised 2024; abstract/metadata inspected; not a current-model benchmark.

title: Efficient Few-Shot Learning Without Prompts
research_note: SetFit trains a sentence-transformer representation contrastively and fits a classification head with few labels. Useful counterexample to the claim that few-shot sentiment requires a large prompt-based model.
qualification: Core efficiency reference; 2022 preprint; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: TweetEval: Unified Benchmark and Comparative Evaluation for Tweet Classification
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2020
research_note: Unifies tweet classification tasks, including sentiment, under standardized datasets and evaluation. Useful for social-domain testing and task distinctions.
qualification: Benchmark paper; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: GoEmotions: A Dataset of Fine-Grained Emotions
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
research_note: Fine-grained emotion dataset. Helps distinguish positive/negative sentiment from a richer emotion taxonomy.
qualification: Dataset paper; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
research_note: Capability-oriented behavioral tests for NLP models. Useful foundation for negation, invariance, and other diagnostic slices beyond aggregate accuracy.
qualification: Core evaluation reference; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
research_note: Studies calibration of neural-network confidence and temperature scaling. Useful when probabilities control human review or model escalation.
qualification: General calibration paper; abstract/metadata inspected; calibration under shift still needs testing.

title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design or: How I learned to start worrying about prompt formatting
research_note: Studies sensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt formatting. Useful for explaining why prompt choice is an experimental variable and why a single template can mislead.
qualification: 2023 preprint / ICLR 2024; abstract/metadata inspected; largest reported effects are not universal sentiment effects.

title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance
research_note: A large domain-oriented language model trained for financial tasks. Useful for explaining financial domain pretraining and broad evaluation.
qualification: 2023 preprint; abstract/metadata inspected; not evidence of a currently available best sentiment system.

title: FinGPT: Open-Source Financial Large Language Models
research_note: Open-source financial LLM framework and adaptation direction. Useful background for instruction-tuned financial models and financial data pipelines.
qualification: 2023 preprint; abstract/metadata inspected; implementation is R33.

title: SemEval-2017 Task 5: Fine-Grained Sentiment Analysis on Financial Microblogs and News
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation (SemEval-2017)
research_note: Fine-grained financial sentiment task using microblogs and news. Useful for target-linked sentiment, continuous scores, and official financial task metrics.
qualification: Benchmark/task paper; abstract/metadata inspected.

title: Large Language Model Adaptation for Financial Sentiment Analysis
research_note: Investigates financial adaptation of foundation models below 1.5B parameters using financial text, instructions, and augmentation. Shows why domain adaptation and model size should be separate variables.
qualification: 2024 preprint; methods/results/limitations inspected; findings depend on its training and evaluation setup.

title: BESSTIE: A Benchmark for Sentiment and Sarcasm Classification for Varieties of English
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
research_note: BESSTIE evaluates sentiment and sarcasm across Australian, Indian, and British English. Useful contemporary evidence on cross-variety generalization and annotation limitations.
qualification: Core recent reading; ACL Findings 2025; methods/results/limitations inspected; sentiment task is binary.

title: Comparing LLMs for Sentiment Analysis in Financial Market News
research_note: Financial comparison across several datasets, with both generative and encoder models. Useful as a critical-reading case: mixed taxonomy, omitted strong linear baselines, and a label-description inconsistency.
qualification: 2025 preprint; methods/results inspected; use cautiously, as discussed in the integrated research and evidence audit notes.

title: Uncovering Sentiment Analysis Circuit in Large Language Model
venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
research_note: Uses sparse autoencoders and circuit interventions to study why sentiment information can be represented internally yet elicited inconsistently by different prompts. Useful current evidence on robustness and mechanistic interpretability.
qualification: Core recent reading; ACL 2026; methods/results/limitations inspected; specific open-weight models and binary-filtered tasks.

Beyond Benchmark Accuracy: Robustness Evaluation of Hinglish Sentiment Models
venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
research_note: Diagnostic Hinglish sentiment study comparing in-distribution, adversarial, and cross-domain results. Supports stress testing but contains a chance-baseline description error and limited evaluation scope.
qualification: 2026 workshop paper; methods/results/limitations inspected; supplementary evidence, not a decisive ranking.

title: When Is a Liability Not a Liability? Textual Analysis, Dictionaries, and 10‐Ks
research_note: Original financial dictionary paper showing the mismatch between general negative word lists and financial language. Important domain-validity motivation.
qualification: Journal of Finance, 2011; publisher-supplied abstract/metadata via Crossref inspected; full paper not reviewed.

title: Giving Content to Investor Sentiment: The Role of Media in the Stock Market
research_note: Historical study of media pessimism and market prices/volume. Motivates financial text measurement while leaving modern causal and trading claims to separate evaluation.
qualification: Journal of Finance, 2007; publisher-supplied abstract/metadata via Crossref inspected; full paper not reviewed.

title: SentiWordNet 3.0: An Enhanced Lexical Resource for Sentiment Analysis and Opinion Mining
venue: Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC'10)
research_note: Word-sense-aware lexicon assigning sentiment/objectivity scores to WordNet synsets. Extends the lexicon taxonomy beyond surface word lookup.
qualification: LREC 2010; primary abstract/metadata inspected; no local word-sense implementation run.
integration: user-contributed research additions; primary sources independently checked

title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2020
research_note: Transformer distillation at pretraining and task stages. Its four-layer student reports over 96.8% of BERT-Base GLUE performance, 7.5-times smaller size and 9.4-times faster inference in the original setup.
qualification: EMNLP Findings 2020; abstract/metadata inspected; historical GLUE and efficiency figures are not universal sentiment accuracy or current timings.
integration: user-contributed research additions; primary sources independently checked

title: Benchmarking large language models for target-based financial sentiment and stock return
venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
research_note: Target-aware Bloomberg financial sentiment benchmark reporting five-shot DeepSeek-R1 macro F1 of 0.87, on 1,334 target cases from 1,162 articles. Adds complementary LLM evidence with dataset, serving, and reporting limitations.
qualification: Published online 2 July 2026, with a December issue date and an earlier 2025 conference version. Full publisher HTML methods/results inspected; Table 3 has an accuracy/weighted-recall inconsistency for one baseline configuration; no local reproduction.
integration: user-contributed research additions; primary sources independently checked
publication_date_basis: Publisher online publication date; citation metadata issue date preserved separately.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
research_note: Official framework describing contextual trustworthiness tradeoffs, including validity, reliability, transparency, interpretability, privacy, and fairness.
qualification: NIST AI RMF 1.0, January 2023; official section 3 and publication page inspected. Voluntary framework, not a sentiment benchmark or model-family prescription.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis for Open-Ended HR Survey Responses
venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Natural Language Processing for Human Resources (NLP4HR 2024)
research_note: Aspect-based sentiment application using 1,458 Dutch HR survey responses and Dutch BERT-based few-shot approaches. Adds an industrial survey application with multiple feedback aspects.
qualification: NLP4HR 2024; abstract/metadata inspected. Independently identified; not assumed to match the missing survey citation in the user draft.
